facts.raw_span: a one-week history of epigastric pain
hematemesis
no significant medical or surgical history
took no medications
a smoker
did not drink alcohol
vital signs were stable
the abdomen was soft without tenderness
a rectal examination revealed no melena
a hemoglobin level of 6.3 g/dL
Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT revealed a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass measuring 6×5 cm with fat attenuation in the antropyloric region

concepts.why: The patient has a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa and a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass measuring 6×5 cm with fat attenuation in the antropyloric region, which is consistent with a gastric lipoma.
The patient has hematemesis and a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa, which is consistent with a gastric ulcer.
The patient has hematemesis and a low hemoglobin level, which is consistent with gastrointestinal bleeding.
The patient has a low hemoglobin level, which is consistent with iron deficiency anemia.
The patient has a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum, which could be a gastric polyp.
The patient has a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass measuring 6×5 cm with fat attenuation in the antropyloric region, which could be a gastric carcinoma.

rationales.F01: Epigastric pain is a non-specific symptom that can be associated with various gastric conditions.
rationales.F02: Hematemesis is a significant symptom that suggests active gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F05: Smoking is a risk factor for gastric ulcers and gastric carcinoma.
rationales.F10: A low hemoglobin level indicates significant blood loss, which is consistent with gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F11: The presence of a submucosal lesion with ulceration in the gastric antrum is highly suggestive of a gastric lipoma.
rationales.F12: The CT findings of a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass with fat attenuation are characteristic of a gastric lipoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a submucosal lesion with ulceration of the overlying mucosa and a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass with fat attenuation on CT is most consistent with a gastric lipoma.
